text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: Ontario Hydro's foes sniff blood: Utility's sudden loss of credibility means it can't dictate policy the way it used to
National abuse study launched: Ottawa seeks uniform definition
India celebrates with cheers, tears: Old rebels question what became of glorious ideals in 50 years since independence
Inkatha official defects to ANC: Angry Buthelezi denounces move
Quirky valour hallmark of Games: Young athletes defy formidable odds to comptete at event
Canadian confirmed as oldest person: 116-year old Quebec native shuns meat, alcohol-but smoked into her 90s
Report on Business Section: Showdown looms for Eaton's: Vulture fund adviser warns restructuring plan may be rejected when it's filed in court today
The movie as bus tour: YOU BE THE DRIVER: The curtain rises today on Immersion Studios' new show, which lets viewers hop for a side trip then hop back on.
Talisman finds huge gas pool in Alberta: Uses new technology to drill deep well
London Insurance unloads U.S. unit: Metropolitan paying $525-million
Torstar sells Hebdo Mag stake: CUC makes deal for Paris publisher of classified ad magazines
THE FINANCIAL POST: Vultures cool to Eaton's plan: Adviser to principal debtholders to recommend voting against restructuring plan and calls for payout of 100 cents on the dollar
Molson earnings slide as Miller and Coors stay out of reach
